title: Exact categorical Fisher identity
research_question: Why does a categorical log barrier correspond to Fisher-volume protection?
design: Exact enumeration for K=2,3,10,100 in CPU float64, including a near-boundary policy.
methods: Exact categorical action enumeration.
key_results: All Bartlett, null-direction, reduced determinant, gradient, Hessian, and finite-difference checks passed; the largest documented directional finite-difference error was 2.80e-9 for K=100.
scientific_conclusion: For fixed categorical logits, log det(F_reduced)=sum_a log pi(a), and the barrier restores unlikely actions.
limitations: This is a fixed-input reduced-coordinate identity, not a global neural Fisher determinant.

title: Categorical bandit smoke run
research_question: Does the stochastic bandit pipeline execute deterministically and save valid artifacts?
design: K=10, four runs, 200 updates.
methods: SGB; entropy-SGB; NPG; LB-SGB.
key_results: All required smoke artifacts and finite-run checks completed.
scientific_conclusion: The implementation pipeline was ready for scientific presets.
limitations: Too short and too small for scientific conclusions.

title: Categorical bandit pilot grid
research_question: Do the declared algorithms and diagnostics behave plausibly before the full grid?
design: K in {10,100}, alpha in {0.01,0.1}, ten runs, 2500 updates.
methods: SGB; entropy-SGB; NPG; LB-SGB.
key_results: The pilot exposed NPG over-commitment and support loss at larger K or alpha, while the barrier preserved more interior geometry.
scientific_conclusion: The pilot justified the full paper-grid and barrier-strength experiments.
limitations: Only ten runs and one tenth of the paper horizon.

title: Barrier-strength ablation
research_question: How does barrier strength trade exploration against concentration?
design: K=10, alpha=0.1, T=25000, 100 paired runs; eta in {100,1000,10000} plus SGB.
methods: SGB and three LB-SGB strengths.
key_results: Eta=1000 improved optimal-arm probability over SGB by 0.200, 95% CI [0.098,0.301]. Eta=100 overexplored; eta=10000 resembled unstable SGB. The cumulative-regret difference was unresolved.
scientific_conclusion: A medium barrier strength best balanced support preservation and reward concentration in this declared setting.
limitations: The best eta is environment- and scale-dependent and must not be copied directly to RL.

title: Full categorical bandit paper-grid reproduction
research_question: Does LB-SGB reproduce the paper mechanism across action count and step size?
design: K in {10,100,1000}, alpha in {0.01,0.1}, T=25000, 100 paired runs per cell; 2400 trajectories.
methods: SGB; entropy-SGB; NPG; LB-SGB.
key_results: At alpha=0.1, optimal-arm probability was SGB/LB-SGB: 0.769/0.955 for K=10, 0.250/0.623 for K=100, and 0.050/0.127 for K=1000. At K=100, LB-SGB had about 93 times the minimum probability and a normalized log-Fisher-volume advantage of 4.622 [4.495,4.749].
scientific_conclusion: Support preservation and continued correction were reproduced strongly for K=10 and K=100; K=1000 remained only partially solved.
limitations: At K=1000 the barrier still selected the wrong modal arm in 82% of runs and incurred more cumulative regret through continued exploration.

title: Exact two-state mathematical verification
research_question: Are the return, pooled weighting, Fisher decomposition, and six barrier gradients implemented exactly?
design: CPU float64 exact trajectory and action enumeration, autograd cross-checks, and finite differences.
methods: Exact analytical formulas versus independent enumeration/autograd.
key_results: All declared checks passed; representative reward-gradient error was 1.39e-17 and full-barrier finite-difference error was 5.37e-11.
scientific_conclusion: The implementation cleanly distinguishes detached conditional, complete weighted, uniform action, visitation, and full pooled-Fisher objectives.
limitations: Verification establishes algebra and code consistency, not empirical superiority.

title: Six exact objectives in the two-state trap MDP
research_question: What changes when categorical action geometry and policy-dependent state visitation are separated?
design: Alpha=0.05, 2000 exact-gradient updates; beta in {0.01,0.1,0.2}; uniform and adverse starts, plus magnitude, step-size, and basin controls.
methods: Reward only; detached conditional; complete weighted; uniform action; visitation only; full pooled Fisher.
key_results: At adverse start and beta=0.1, final (J,q,p_good) was reward-only (0.491,0.002,0.016), detached conditional (0.401,0.248,0.309), uniform action (0.565,0.533,0.699), visitation only (0.419,0.192,0.017), and full pooled Fisher (0.785,0.830,0.866).
scientific_conclusion: Conditional action protection and visitation pressure are distinct directions; combining them improved recovery in this exact declared comparison.
limitations: The full objective also adds reward-independent visitation bias; disjoint tabular parameters do not transfer directly to shared neural networks.

title: Sampled two-state pilot
research_question: Does the finite-batch implementation reproduce the exact estimator identities and train stably?
design: Twenty seeds, full 2000 updates, and 5000 audit batches.
methods: Sampled REINFORCE with five oracle barriers and one practical sampled conditional barrier.
key_results: The pilot reproduced finite-batch ratio bias, zero-downstream-state batches, and convergence toward the conditional oracle.
scientific_conclusion: The full 100-seed estimator audit and training grid was justified.
limitations: Pilot Monte Carlo precision and seed count are lower than the full preset.

title: Finite-batch estimator audit
research_question: How do random transition counts affect state weights, conditional gradients, and the undamped empirical Fisher?
design: Five fixed policies; N in {1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256}; exact binomial moments and 50000 Monte Carlo batches per cell.
methods: Population targets versus sampled state weights, sampled conditional gradients, reward gradients, and empirical Fishers.
key_results: For the adverse policy, P(no s1) was 0.938 at N=4 and 0.599 at N=32; at N=32 only 2.388% of empirical Fishers were full rank with a defined ordinary log determinant. Conditional-gradient bias decreased with N.
scientific_conclusion: Rare-state batches can remove direct state protection entirely even when the estimator is asymptotically consistent.
limitations: Undamped empirical log determinants are often undefined; no spectral floor was added.

title: Full sampled two-state training grid
research_question: How does the practical sampled conditional barrier compare with exact regularizer controls during sampled learning?
design: Alpha=0.05, 2000 updates, beta in {0.01,0.1,0.2}, N in {4,32,128}, two starts, 100 paired seeds.
methods: Reward only; five exact oracle regularizers; sampled detached conditional barrier.
key_results: At adverse start, N=32, beta=0.1, sampled conditional reached (J,q,p_good)=(0.400,0.246,0.302), close to its oracle (0.402,0.248,0.311). Their paired return gap shrank from -0.01324 at N=4 to -0.000407 at N=128.
scientific_conclusion: The practical sampled estimator approaches the population conditional target as batch size grows but does not reproduce explicit visitation pressure.
limitations: Return differences do not prove Fisher geometry is causal, and the oracle visitation/full methods are not ordinary neural-rollout estimators.

title: Temporary sampled conditional barrier
research_question: After a practical barrier moves the adverse policy out of the safe basin, can reward-only learning finish the task?
design: N=32, alpha=0.05, 4000 updates, 100 paired seeds; sampled barrier beta=0.2 until update 2000 and zero afterward.
methods: Reward only; fixed sampled conditional; sampled conditional handoff; full-oracle handoff diagnostic.
key_results: At adverse start, final return was 0.495 reward-only, 0.619 fixed barrier, 0.979 sampled handoff, and 0.981 full-oracle handoff. The practical handoff ended at q=0.987 and p_good=0.989.
scientific_conclusion: Temporary conditional protection can move the policy into a basin where ordinary reward optimization becomes self-sustaining.
limitations: The exact full-oracle handoff is an upper reference, not the practical candidate algorithm.

title: Handoff switch-time robustness
research_question: Was update 2000 accidentally an ideal handoff time?
design: N=32, beta=0.2, 4000 updates, 100 paired seeds; switch in {500,1000,1500,2000,2500}.
methods: Five temporary sampled-conditional schedules.
key_results: At adverse start, switch 500 failed with final J=0.494, while switches 1000,1500,2000,2500 reached J=0.983,0.983,0.979,0.973 respectively.
scientific_conclusion: The result is robust across a broad successful switch window but exhibits a transition between updates 500 and 1000.
limitations: This is a narrow schedule robustness check, not a broad hyperparameter search.

title: Focused handoff-threshold post-hoc analysis
research_question: What condition is present at successful switches 1000/1500 but absent at failed switch 500?
design: Archive-based policy reconstruction at switch, +50,+100,+250,+500, and final checkpoints, with reward-vector-field counterfactual continuations.
methods: Switch schedules 500,1000,1500, with 2000/2500 endpoint controls.
key_results: Behavioral quantities and the exact reward-only vector field changed across the transition; improved Fisher geometry accompanied it but was not a unique explanatory threshold.
scientific_conclusion: The most defensible explanation is a behavioral/reward-gradient feedback threshold that makes post-handoff learning self-sustaining.
limitations: Post-hoc checkpoint associations cannot establish geometric causality.

title: Neural discrete smoke and original Acrobot pilot
research_question: Does the neural conditional barrier execute, and does the original Acrobot setup learn at all?
design: CartPole smoke followed by a short Acrobot learning-rate pilot.
methods: Reward-only and regularized neural categorical policies.
key_results: CartPole completed finitely; all original Acrobot candidates ended at -500.
scientific_conclusion: The barrier pipeline worked, but Acrobot required a learning-capable baseline before any comparison.
limitations: The Acrobot pilot is superseded and cannot be used as evidence against GPOMDP or the barrier.

title: Initial Acrobot negative confirmatory gate
research_question: Did the first fixed-budget neural comparison demonstrate a barrier effect?
design: Ten seeds and the original interaction-budget collector, with GPOMDP variants and NPG.
methods: Reward-only; fixed entropy; fixed barrier; handoff barrier; NPG.
key_results: Every method and seed ended at deterministic return -500; fixed-reference spectra differed little across GPOMDP variants.
scientific_conclusion: No barrier conclusion was possible because reward-only GPOMDP also failed; the stage motivated baseline repair.
limitations: Superseded protocol; do not combine its endpoints with the later complete-episode experiments.

title: Acrobot GPOMDP learning-rate selection
research_question: Which learning rate makes reward-only GPOMDP reliably learn before introducing a regularizer?
design: Rates 1e-4 through 1e-2 screened for 300 updates; best two continued to 1000 updates.
methods: Reward-only GPOMDP only.
key_results: Learning rate 0.003 was selected for confirmation under complete-episode updates.
scientific_conclusion: This isolates regularizer effects from a broken reward-only baseline.
limitations: Small pilot cohorts select a configuration; they are not method-effect estimates.

title: Five-seed GPOMDP baseline gate
research_question: Does the selected reward-only configuration learn Acrobot reliably enough to authorize ablations?
design: Five new seeds, lr=0.003, 1000 updates, 8000 complete episodes per seed.
methods: Reward-only GPOMDP.
key_results: Median final stochastic return -86.656; termination rate 1.0; mean improvement 409.213 [394.822,423.603]; all five seeds improved by at least 100.
scientific_conclusion: The predeclared baseline gate passed and regularizer experiments became interpretable.
limitations: Five seeds establish viability, not a precise catastrophic-failure rate.

title: Independent regularizer coefficient calibration
research_question: How can entropy and barrier scales be chosen without outcome tuning?
design: Five disjoint early-policy seeds; match median scaled regularizer norm to 0.3 times reward-gradient norm.
methods: Conditional log barrier and entropy.
key_results: Selected barrier beta=546.4135159 and entropy coefficient=588.8195483 without inspecting final reward outcomes.
scientific_conclusion: Initial gradient-norm matching provides a declared scale control for the ablation.
limitations: It equalizes initial norm, not direction, objective meaning, or later gradient magnitude.

title: Five-seed neural regularizer ablation
research_question: Do permanent entropy/barrier controls or a temporary barrier improve on the validated baseline?
design: Five paired seeds, lr=0.003, 1000 updates; handoff after 25%.
methods: Reward only; fixed entropy; fixed barrier; 25% barrier handoff.
key_results: Mean final stochastic returns were -168.431, -246.844, -251.319, and -88.006 respectively. Reward-only failed on 1/5; handoff on 0/5.
scientific_conclusion: The temporary schedule was promising, while permanent regularization imposed persistent exploration cost.
limitations: Five-seed paired intervals were wide; this was a mechanism pilot.

title: Seed 402 paired divergence audit
research_question: Did the barrier prevent a collapse unique to one failed reward-only seed?
design: Every stored checkpoint for seed 402 and successful control seed 403; on-policy and fixed-reference Fishers.
methods: Reward only versus 25% barrier handoff.
key_results: The methods diverged in behavior and action support, but no single Fisher-rank or determinant threshold explained success.
scientific_conclusion: The audit supported an optimization-basin interpretation and motivated a larger reliability cohort.
limitations: Outcome-selected case study; not a population causal estimate.

title: Twenty-seed reliability confirmation
research_question: Does the temporary barrier reduce seed-level catastrophic failures beyond the five-seed pilot?
design: Twenty paired primary seeds; fixed controls on ten seeds; 1000 updates and 25% handoff.
methods: Reward only; handoff primary; fixed entropy and fixed barrier secondary.
key_results: Reward-only failed 2/20 and handoff 0/20. Mean final return was -129.366 versus -89.433; paired difference +39.933 [-20.221,100.087].
scientific_conclusion: The failure pattern persisted descriptively and justified the frozen extension to 60 pairs.
limitations: The paired return interval included zero and failure events were still few.

title: Final 60-pair Acrobot reliability extension
research_question: Under the frozen protocol, does a 25% temporary barrier reduce catastrophic failure?
design: Sixty paired seeds, lr=0.003, 1000 updates, 8000 complete episodes, centered unnormalized returns, beta=546.414 until update 250.
methods: Reward-only GPOMDP versus temporary conditional categorical log barrier.
key_results: Failures were 8/60 (13.33%, Wilson [6.91%,24.17%]) versus 2/60 (3.33%, [0.92%,11.36%]). Paired failure difference -0.100 [-0.203,0.003]; exact McNemar p=0.109375. Final-return difference was +39.029 [-3.227,81.285]; AUC difference +1.116 [-25.390,27.622].
scientific_conclusion: The handoff produced a large descriptive reliability improvement, but the primary paired inference remained statistically unresolved and there was no general AUC benefit.
limitations: The result is promising rather than conclusive; two reward-only successes were harmed by handoff.

title: Final discordant-seed mechanism analysis
research_question: What differs in seeds where reward-only and handoff disagree on catastrophic failure?
design: All ten discordant seeds, both methods, reference-bank action distributions, margins, disagreement states, visitation frequencies, and return milestones.
methods: Eight reward-failed/handoff-succeeded pairs and two reward-succeeded/handoff-failed pairs.
key_results: Handoff rescued seeds 512,517,532,538,542,550,557,560 but harmed 545 and 556. Seed 556 showed harmful suppression of useful specialization; seed 545 showed a late reward-only escape.
scientific_conclusion: Temporary support protection changes the optimization basin and can either rescue exploration or delay useful specialization.
limitations: Selected on outcome discordance; descriptive and noncausal.

title: Legacy fixed-segment collector quarantine
research_question: Why are some early Acrobot artifacts excluded?
design: Legacy fixed-length segments that prematurely truncated episodes.
methods: Early neural pilot methods.
key_results: The implementation flaw was documented and the artifacts were retained only for auditability.
scientific_conclusion: No outcome from this collector enters the scientific synthesis.
limitations: Invalid for scientific comparison.
